Mysliborz Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Myślibórz, Poland

Demolished. Myślibórz's Jewish community, numbering about 120 people in the 1840s, had dwindled to about 30 within a century. This cemetery, probably established in the 18th century, functioned until the end of the 1930s and, remarkably, was not destroyed under Nazi rule at all; photographic documentation from 1963 confirms it remained in good condition, wooded, with numerous legible German- and Hebrew-inscribed tombstones still standing at that late date. Its destruction must therefore have occurred sometime after 1963; it was formally excluded from conservation records in 1992, and private residential buildings now occupy the site.
